original_question: For every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1, determine whether the invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is always strictly greater than 1/r^2.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.3: the open problem asking whether the strict odd-order bound ms(G,r)>1/r^2 holds for every group of odd order and every r>1, in the finite-group setting of Section 4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct target very closely: the finite-group invariant ms(G,r), the class of odd-order groups, the quantifier over all integers r>1, and the strict threshold 1/r^2 that is exactly at issue in Question 4.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
missing_details: The paper’s notion of symmetry should be stated explicitly: a subset A⊂G is symmetric if A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

To make the problem fully stand-alone, one should define MS(G,r) first as the least upper bound of the cardinal numbers t such that every r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic symmetric subset of size at least t, and then set ms(G,r)=MS(G,r)/|G| for finite G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
The coloring quantifier should be written explicitly, e.g. as every map χ:G→{1,…,r}; this is implicit in the paper’s phrase “every r-coloring.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

The paper phrases this as a yes/no question (“Is it true that ...?”), so that is slightly closer to the official formulation than the broader wording “determine whether.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

The nearby context matters for fidelity: Section 4 first records a non-strict bound ms(G,r)≥1/r^2 for odd-order groups, then Theorem 4.2 proves the strict inequality for Abelian odd-order groups, and Question 4.3 asks whether that strict improvement extends to all odd-order groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
refined_question: Let G be a finite group of odd order, and let r>1 be an integer. Define MS(G,r) to be the least upper bound of all cardinal numbers t such that every coloring χ:G→{1,…,r} contains a monochromatic subset A⊂G with A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G and |A|≥t, and set ms(G,r):=MS(G,r)/|G|. Is it true that ms(G,r)>1/r^2 for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r>1? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is it true that for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r>1, every r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic symmetric subset A⊂G with |A|>|G|/r^2, where symmetric means A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
justification: This is the paper’s Section 4, Question 4.3 rather than a broader neighboring problem. Section 4 introduces MS(G,r) and its normalized version ms(G,r) for finite groups, the remark after Theorem 4.1 gives the known non-strict odd-order lower bound, Theorem 4.2 proves the strict inequality for Abelian groups of odd order, and Question 4.3 asks whether the same strict inequality holds for all odd-order groups. There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions here; the hidden assumptions are purely group-theoretic and are exactly the ones made explicit in the refined question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
